analysis.title: Weekly guidance from our Investment Strategy Committee, October 26, 2026
key_insights: Wells Fargo remains favorable on commodities but expects the pace of gains to moderate in 2027 after a 35% year-to-date rise as of October 20, because higher real rates raise the hurdle. It would use pullbacks to add exposure.

The Bloomberg Commodity Index is at multi-year highs even though the 10-year inflation-adjusted Treasury yield rose to a multi-year high of 2.9%. History shows real yields and commodity returns are negatively correlated over the long run, but there are periods of decoupling.

Firm demand meets supply constraints: US Q2 real GDP grew 2.2% y/y, September S&P Global US Manufacturing PMI is the strongest since 2022, Eurozone Composite PMIs are at a three-and-a-half year high, and China's official factory measure returned to expansion.

In energy, about 40% of Middle East exports bypass the Strait of Hormuz through fragmented routes. Refining remains significantly hindered by damaged Middle East and Russian capacity, so global refinery runs are well below 2025 and fuel prices are likely to stay elevated. Multi-year low oil and fuel inventories also need to be rebuilt.
AI buildout is creating secular demand for energy, copper and other metals. The IEA estimates copper demand could exceed supply by nearly 30% by 2035 because mined supply is sluggish.

The 10-year Treasury yield is near 5%, more than one percentage point above its February 27, 2026 low. The equity risk premium (S&P 500 earnings yield minus the 10-year yield) is near the low end of its 25-year range.

Wells Fargo's year-end 2027 target for the 10-year Treasury is 5.25%-5.75%, which could push the equity risk premium below zero for the first time since 2002. It argues a negative premium is not a bearish signal: the premium crossed zero multiple times in the 1990s when the S&P 500 returned about 18.2% annualized.

Wells Fargo says equities remain attractive in a higher-rate environment because corporate profits continue to grow at an impressive rate. It says the equity risk premium is not a reliable market-timing signal.

France's bond selloff is framed as a warning for developed-market bonds. France's 2025 budget deficit was 5.1% of GDP, well above the EU average, and its yields have risen more than other developed markets in 2026.

Italy plans higher spending, Spain's November election adds budget uncertainty, and Japanese yields are rising. Wells Fargo stays unfavorable on developed-market ex-US fixed income because yields below US levels offer less income against rising fiscal and political risk.
Wells Fargo believes US Treasuries should keep investor demand because of US economic strength and the Treasury market's central role, though it acknowledges US fiscal and political risks.

Private equity's recovery through Q3 is uneven. Deal value moderated but deal count rose, buyouts picked up after a soft Q2, and venture capital is on pace for a record year with over $500B invested through Q3, about 45% above the 2021 full-year record.

Private markets are highly concentrated: AI startups took over 80% of US venture deal value through Q3, and the largest 5% of deals made up roughly 75% of Q3 deal value. Nearly 1,000 unicorns hold a combined $5.7T valuation, but only 18 VC-backed companies went public in Q3.
Wells Fargo says higher rates could raise financing costs and limit exits. It prefers secondaries, growth equity, and small- and mid-buyouts.

risk_factors: Higher real interest rates raise the hurdle for commodities.
Refining constraints and low oil and fuel inventories keep fuel prices elevated.
A negative equity risk premium would remove the upfront yield premium for holding equities.
Fiscal and political risks across developed-market sovereign bonds, including France, Italy, Spain and Japan.
US Treasuries also face fiscal risks and political uncertainty.
Higher rates could raise private equity financing costs and constrain exits.
Private market concentration in AI and large deals, with a large backlog of unicorns awaiting exits.

geopolitical: Middle East oil exports are recovering unevenly, with 40% of exports bypassing the Strait of Hormuz through fragmented routes and disruption risks lingering.
Damage to Middle East and Russian refining capacity and export restrictions are keeping global refinery runs below 2025 levels.
French political division and rising debt are pushing French bond yields higher.
Spain's November election adds political uncertainty to the budget outlook.
Italy plans to increase spending, and governments are balancing higher defense and energy spending with stretched public finances.

tension_points.bull_case: A negative equity risk premium is not a warning. The premium crossed zero repeatedly in the 1990s when the S&P 500 returned about 18.2% annualized, and equity returns can benefit from earnings growth, productivity, dividends and buybacks.
tension_points.bear_case: With the 10-year near 5% and a year-end 2027 target of 5.25%-5.75%, the equity risk premium could turn negative for the first time since 2002, leaving investors no upfront yield premium for equity volatility and potential losses.

tension_points.bull_case: Firm economic activity, supply constraints, refining bottlenecks and AI-driven metals demand have kept commodities at multi-year highs despite a 2.9% real 10-year yield.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher or rising real yields have historically coincided with weaker commodity prices over the long run, and the report expects gains to moderate in 2027.

theme_stances.key_argument: Firm demand and supply constraints explain why commodities have stayed resilient despite higher real rates, though gains should moderate in 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: we continue to favor commodities and would use pullbacks
